decisions.evidence: Maker R1 proposed “Save a bookmark — Enter an address ... it’s validated and persisted”; Client R1 called the draft a good start and requested additions without disputing URL-based saving.
decisions.note: The initial specification conformed to saving a bookmark by entering a URL.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 offered only an “auto-derived” title; Client R1 required automatic collection of “title, description, icon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the client supplied the missing metadata-capture requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 described an optional title and later fixing titles; Client R1 required collected “title and description” to remain editable.
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the proposal did not cover editable collected descriptions, and the client added the conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 limited edit behavior to “Fix titles/addresses”; Client R1 added editable descriptions, bookmark notes, and tag management.
decisions.note: Initial specification review: editing was limited to only part of the bookmark fields, and the client extended the scope to the missing fields.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 proposed “Edit & delete” and “delete with a confirmation step”; Client R1 did not reject deletion and later distinguished it from reversible archiving.
decisions.note: The presented delete behavior conformed to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 said duplicate addresses were covered as an edge case; Client R1 identified the proposed behavior as “merely warning” and required opening the existing bookmark for editing.
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the client replaced the divergent duplicate-warning behavior with convergence on editing the existing item.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 only proposed “See your list”; Client R1 required “A readable list showing the title, description, tags, and site icon.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the client supplied the missing readability and per-item field requirements.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 proposed “open in a new tab”; Client R1 did not object to the original-link opening behavior.
decisions.note: Opening a bookmark’s original URL in a new tab is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 proposed “Label bookmarks”; Client R1 retained tags and asked only that they be moved earlier and enhanced.
decisions.note: Assigning tags was already present; its priority was orthogonal to the reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1’s tag story only said “Label bookmarks and filter by tag”; Client R1 requested “Existing-tag suggestions while adding tags.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: autocomplete from existing tags was missing and explicitly added.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 proposed “filter by tag”; Client R1 retained that tag behavior.
decisions.note: The presented tag filtering behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 proposed only “search by keyword”; Client R1 required search across “titles, descriptions, notes, and addresses,” including note text.
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the client supplied the missing full-text field coverage.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 described generic keyword search; Client R1 explicitly required “Case-insensitive search.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: case-insensitive matching was missing and added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 described generic keyword search; Client R1 requested search “including `#tag`.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: tag-query syntax was absent and the client added it.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 described generic keyword search; Client R1 requested “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: Boolean operators and grouped expressions were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 described generic keyword search; Client R1 requested “exact phrases.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: quoted exact-phrase search was missing and explicitly added.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1’s four-story scope contained no read-later state; Client R1 requested “Read-later status.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: unread/read-later state was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no unread perspective; Client R1 requested “a separate unread view.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the client added the missing unread-only view.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no read-state action; Client R1 requested “the ability to mark items read.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: marking an unread bookmark as read was missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no bulk operations; Client R1 requested selecting multiple bookmarks “to tag, mark read or unread, archive, or delete.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the client added multi-selection and the required bulk-action categories; tag removal was refined in a later decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no collection-wide bulk operation; Client R1 requested acting on “everything matching the current view.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the client added current-filter-scoped whole-collection actions.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no sorting story; Client R1 requested “Sorting by useful choices such as date added and title.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: configurable sort keys were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no note feature; Client R1 requested “Notes on bookmarks, with simple formatting and note text included in search.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: formatted bookmark notes and their rendered/searchable use were missing.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no saved-copy feature; Client R1 requested “A saved local copy of the page, storing the PDF itself when the link is a PDF.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the client added local snapshots and the PDF exception; the exact HTML packaging was refined later.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no external preservation feature; Client R1 requested “an option to preserve it through the Internet Archive.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: Internet Archive preservation was missing and added.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no archive feature; Client R1 requested reversible archiving with archived items “hidden from normal lists and searches.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the client added reversible archive behavior and default/search exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 only proposed deletion; Client R1 required archiving “as a reversible action, separate from permanent deletion.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the client added the archive/delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 omitted archiving entirely; Client R1 requested reversible archiving and hiding archived items but did not state the expectation for a separate archived-only list. Maker R5 later presented “archive view.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: the separate archive-list requirement was not surfaced in the client’s response. Its later conforming appearance does not retroactively establish capture.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no bundle/saved-filter feature; Client R1 requested “Saved searches that can combine text with included and excluded tags.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: reusable saved filters were missing and explicitly added.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no import feature; Client R1 requested “Import ... using the common browser-bookmark HTML format.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: Netscape/browser HTML import was missing; preservation details were refined later.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no export feature; Client R1 requested “export using the common browser-bookmark HTML format.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: Netscape/browser HTML export was missing; preservation details were refined later.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 contained no personal display settings; Client R1 requested “default sorting, number of items shown, and text size.”
decisions.note: Initial specification review: display preferences were missing and explicitly added.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 summarized bulk actions as selecting many or the current view “to tag”; Client R2 corrected that “Bulk tag actions should support both adding and removing tags.”
decisions.note: Second specification review: the revised bulk design still omitted explicit tag removal, which the client supplied.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 specified import in “standard browser-bookmark HTML format” without preservation details; Client R2 required preserving “title, tags, and original date added.”
decisions.note: Second specification review: the import contract lacked required field preservation.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 specified export in “standard browser-bookmark HTML format” without preservation details; Client R2 required preserving “title, tags, and original date added.”
decisions.note: Second specification review: the export contract lacked required field preservation.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 described a “page snapshot” and PDF storage; Client R2 specified that a web-page copy “should be a self-contained local HTML file.”
decisions.note: Second specification review: the client replaced the underspecified snapshot representation with the required single-file HTML outcome.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 listed “`#tag` terms” but did not state their combination rule; Client R2 required ordinary text plus `#tag` to narrow results “using both conditions.”
decisions.note: Second specification review: the client supplied the missing AND semantics between text and tag queries.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 listed `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`/parentheses but omitted quoted-operator handling; Client R2 required quoted words such as `"AND"` to be treated as literal text.
decisions.note: Second specification review: the client added the missing quoted-operator literal rule.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2 interpreted simple formatting as “bold, italics, lists, links”; Client R2 replied that “lightweight Markdown ... is exactly what I meant.”
decisions.note: The note-format clarification conformed to the reference and was explicitly confirmed.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5’s task breakdown explicitly included US7 “reversible archive, archive view”; Client R5 approved the breakdown subject only to unrelated browser-check additions.
decisions.note: At task review, the later recorded archive-view decision conformed to the reference; it is distinct from the earlier unexpressed omission.

decision.evidence: Maker R1 offered A “Single user, no login” or B “Multiple users”; Client R1 selected “Option A: single user with no login.”
decision.note: At the initial specification gate, the alternatives differed from the reference’s single-user scope, and the client selected the conforming option.
